scenes.title:
Claude Connectors
[[Connect Once, Use Everywhere]]
scenes.subtitle: Link Claude to your apps, then use them from Claude Code

lines.say: Do you keep copying things from your other apps into Claude? A bug report from Notion, an email, a meeting from your calendar?
Connectors fix that. You connect an app once, and Claude can read it and act in it, everywhere you use Claude, including Claude Code.
In this video, you'll learn what connectors are, when to use them, and how to set one up and use it, step by step.

scenes.heading: What is a [[connector]]?
items: A **link** between Claude and an outside app: your docs, calendar, email, issue tracker
Claude can **find information** there and **take actions** for you
Built on **MCP**: the service runs an MCP server, the connector links Claude to it

card.title: ONE CONNECTOR, EVERY CLAUDE APP
card.code:
claude.ai on the web   ✓
Claude desktop app     ✓
Claude mobile app      ✓
Claude Code            ✓

lines.say: So, what is a connector?
A connector links Claude to an outside app or service, like your documents, your calendar, your email, or your issue tracker.
Once it's connected, Claude can find information there, and take actions for you.
Under the hood, it's MCP, the Model Context Protocol. The service runs an MCP server, and the connector links Claude to it.
Think of it like signing in to an app on your phone: you do it once, and it's saved to your Claude account, on the web, desktop, mobile, and in Claude Code.

scenes.heading: How a connector [[works]]

rows.label: The service runs an MCP server
rows.text: Notion, Gmail, Google Drive, your issue tracker…

rows.label: You connect it once in claude.ai
rows.text: Pick it in the directory, then sign in to the service

rows.label: Every Claude app can use it
rows.text: Web, desktop, mobile, and Claude Code with the same account

scenes.banner: ✓ Connect once, use it everywhere you sign in

lines.say: Here's how it works, in three parts.
First, the service runs an MCP server. Notion, Gmail, Google Drive, and many others already have one.
Second, you connect it once, in claude.ai. You pick it in the connectors directory, and sign in to the service. No API keys to copy.
Third, it's saved to your account. So every Claude app you sign in to can use it, including Claude Code.
Connect once, use it everywhere.

left.title: Connector (added in claude.ai)

• Apps you sign in to:

  and in Claude Code

right.title: claude mcp add (Claude Code)
right.body:
• Stays on this one machine
• Local tools, like a browser
  for testing (Playwright)
• Shared with your team
  in the project's .mcp.json
• Works with an API key login

lines.say: So when should you use a connector, and when should you add an MCP server directly in Claude Code?
Use a connector for online apps you sign in to, like Notion or Gmail, and that you want in every Claude app.
Use claude mcp add for things that stay on one machine: local tools like a test browser, or servers you share with your team in the project's mcp dot json file.
lines.tts: Use claude M C P add for things that stay on one machine: local tools like a test browser, or servers you share with your team in the project's M C P dot json file.

lines.say: I covered that in my MCP video. Today, we'll do the connector way.
lines.tts: I covered that in my M C P video. Today, we'll do the connector way.

left.title: Before: copy and paste
left.body:
1. Open Notion, find the bug
2. Copy the bug report
3. Paste it into Claude Code
4. Fix it, run the tests
5. Go back, update Notion

…for every bug, every time

right.title: After: one connector
right.body:
"Fix the top bug from our list"

✓ Claude reads Notion itself
✓ Fixes the code
✓ Runs the tests
✓ Asks, then marks it fixed
   in Notion

lines.say: Here's our use case. I run a small online shop, and I keep my bug list in a Notion page.
Before: for every bug, I open Notion, copy the report, paste it into Claude Code, and then go back to update the page.
After: I just say, fix the top bug from our list. Claude reads Notion itself, fixes the code, runs the tests, and asks before it marks the bug as fixed.
Let's see the problem first. Here's my shop project: the cart code, and its tests.
I start Claude Code, and ask it to fix the top bug from my Notion bug list.

do.text: Fix the top bug from my Notion bug list

lines.say: Claude can't see Notion from here. So it asks me to paste the bug report.

lines: ai:I can't access Notion from this session. Could you paste the bug report here?

lines.say: That's the copy and paste loop, for every single bug. Let's fix it, with a connector.
Step one: connect Notion in claude.ai. I go to Customize, then Connectors.

lines.say: That's it. I never copied a key or a token. And this connector is now saved to my Claude account.
Step two: check it in Claude Code.
Claude Code loads your connectors when a session starts. So I start a new session, signed in with the same claude.ai account.
I type slash M C P, to see my MCP servers.
lines.tts: I type slash M C P, to see my M C P servers.

lines.say: There it is: claude dot A I Notion, in its own claude dot A I section. I didn't run a single command to add it.
lines.tts: There it is: Claude dot A I Notion, in its own Claude dot A I section. I didn't run a single command to add it.

lines.say: If you don't see it, run slash status. Connectors only load when you're signed in with a claude.ai subscription, not with an API key.
lines.tts: If you don't see it, run slash status. Connectors only load when you're signed in with a Claude dot A I subscription, not with an API key.

lines.say: Step three: tell Claude where things are.
Claude can use Notion now, but it doesn't know which page holds my bugs. So I add it to CLAUDE.md, the file Claude reads at the start of every session.
lines.tts: Claude can use Notion now, but it doesn't know which page holds my bugs. So I add it to CLAUDE dot M D, the file Claude reads at the start of every session.

do.text:
# my-shop

## Where things are
- Bug reports live in Notion, on the page "my-shop bugs".
  Read them with the Notion connector.
- Tests: python -m pytest -q

lines.say: The bug reports live in Notion, on the page called my-shop bugs. And here's the test command.
Then two rules: fix one bug at a time, and ask before changing anything in Notion. Reading is fine, but changes need my OK.

do.text:
## Rules
- Fix one bug at a time, then run the tests.
- Ask before you change anything in Notion.

lines.say: Step four: use it. Same request as before.

do.text: Fix the top bug from our bug list

lines.say: This time, Claude calls the Notion connector. It searches for the page, then reads it. The top bug: no free shipping at exactly fifty.

lines: res:2 bugs · #1 High: no free shipping at exactly 50

lines.say: Then it reads the cart code, and finds the cause: greater than fifty, instead of greater than or equal to fifty.
Following my CLAUDE.md, it runs the tests. All eight pass.
lines.tts: Following my CLAUDE dot M D, it runs the tests. All eight pass.

lines: ai:Fixed bug #1: shipping is now free from 50, with 50 included. Should I mark it as fixed in Notion?

lines.say: And it asks before touching Notion, just like my rule says. I say yes.
Claude updates the bug in Notion. No copy, no paste, no switching apps.

lines: ai:Done. Bug #1 is marked as fixed in Notion.

lines.say: Step five: control what the connector can do.
In claude.ai, open the connector's page. For each group of tools, you choose: always allow, needs approval, or blocked.
Here, Claude can read freely, but every change needs my approval.
And Disconnect signs Claude out of the service, everywhere.
In Claude Code, you have two more switches.

do.title: Turn connectors off in Claude Code
rows: all of them, for a repo

lines.say: In slash M C P, you can turn one connector off for this project only. And a setting called disable Claude A I connectors turns them all off, for example in a repo that should never touch your apps.

cards.title: Connect what you trust
cards.text: Verified, Community or Custom: check the label

cards.title: Not in Claude Code?
cards.text: Run `/status`: use a claude.ai login, not an API key

cards.title: Not in the directory?
cards.text: Add a custom connector with its server URL

cards.title: Team plan?
cards.text: An Owner adds it, then you connect your own account

lines.say: Before you connect more apps, four tips.
One: only connect services you trust. The label shows how much Anthropic reviewed a connector: Verified, Community, or Custom, which means you added it yourself.
Two: if a connector doesn't show up in Claude Code, run slash status, and make sure you're signed in with your claude.ai account.
lines.tts: Two: if a connector doesn't show up in Claude Code, run slash status, and make sure you're signed in with your Claude dot A I account.

lines.say: Three: if an app isn't in the directory, but it has a remote MCP server, add it as a custom connector, with its URL.
lines.tts: Three: if an app isn't in the directory, but it has a remote M C P server, add it as a custom connector, with its URL.

lines.say: And four: on a Team or Enterprise plan, an Owner adds the connector for everyone. Then each person connects their own account.

scenes.heading: Recap
items: A connector links Claude to an app: it can **read** and **act** there
Connect it **once** in claude.ai, use it in **every** Claude app
Point Claude to your data in `CLAUDE.md`, and [[control the tools]]

lines.say: Let's recap.
A connector links Claude to an outside app, so it can find information there, and act for you.
You connect it once in claude.ai, and it works in every Claude app, including Claude Code.
lines.tts: You connect it once in Claude dot A I, and it works in every Claude app, including Claude Code.

lines.say: Then tell Claude where your data lives in CLAUDE.md, and choose which tools need your approval.
lines.tts: Then tell Claude where your data lives in CLAUDE dot M D, and choose which tools need your approval.
